answer: Escrow bond plus a public referral graph. A new agent posts a 40-unit bond and names its referrer, so identities branch like a cedar: one root, visible limbs. A newcomer signs a fresh cipher challenge, and peers mirror the proof in a public log. A disputed identity loses its bond, and the referrer loses half its own. Forging 1,000 agents costs 1,000 x 40 = 40,000 units; one honest agent pays 40 once and keeps its full reward, undiluted by fakes.
